included: current and historical plans/HANDOFF/issues relevant to current-step continuity
excluded_from_deficiency_ownership: actual MinIO/S3 live behavior because user deferred live testing

overall_assessment.reason: P0 corrective and pre-production boundaries should be selected explicitly; MinIO-dependent Artifact work remains deferred.

findings.title: Current Runtime plan SOT is stale and the current-document regression does not validate each SOT independently
evidence: okcanvas-agent-runtime/PLANS.md still declares STEP091B3R1 / 2.74.1 and real PostgreSQL pending
root PLANS.md declares STEP008R4R7 / STEP091D / 2.75.0 and parent real PostgreSQL 19/19 accepted
tests/test_workspace_step008r4r1_document_plan_and_storage_audit.py omits okcanvas-agent-runtime/PLANS.md from current docs and concatenates multiple docs before checking CURRENT_STEP
docs/plans/OKCANVAS_AGENT_RUNTIME_PRODUCTIZATION_MASTER_PLAN.md immediate backlog still stops at STEP091C-era wording
findings.impact: A ZIP-only continuation can choose the wrong baseline or reopen an already accepted PostgreSQL gate.
findings.recommended_closure: Synchronize current plans/issue registry and replace combined-document assertions with per-file current-identity assertions driven from one machine-readable current-baseline SOT.

findings.title: Admin and multi-user Service APIs share one FastAPI listener while loopback-only admin traffic is not physically enforced
evidence: bootstrap/application.py constructs one FastAPI app and registers both Service and Admin routers
transport/admin/rest/auth.py enforces only static header credentials, not loopback source or listener isolation
scripts/windows_entrypoint.py accepts OKCANVAS_API_HOST and defaults to 127.0.0.1 but validate_control_api_environment does not reject a non-loopback host
docs/00-CONSTITUTION.md states credential-bearing operator traffic is loopback-only
findings.impact: The default loopback bind is safe, but an external bind required for a multi-user Service API would also expose Admin routes on that listener, contrary to the documented boundary.
findings.recommended_closure: Prefer separate external Service and loopback Admin listeners/processes. At minimum add explicit fail-closed loopback enforcement for Admin traffic and an acceptance gate for non-loopback binding.

findings.title: Real PostgreSQL works on a fresh schema but there is no versioned production migration lifecycle
evidence: PostgreSQL adapters initialize with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS
product_store.py records schema_migration version 1 but there is no ordered first-party migration runner
no Alembic/Flyway/Liquibase or first-party migration directory/runner exists in the package
STEP091B3R1 real PostgreSQL acceptance proves fresh/live behavior but explicitly does not execute production database migration
findings.impact: Existing production schemas cannot be safely preflighted, upgraded, rolled forward/back, or audited by ordered schema version.
findings.recommended_closure: Introduce an explicit migration catalog/runner, current schema version, preflight, transactional upgrade policy, backup/rollback requirements and live upgrade acceptance against an older retained schema.

findings.title: Health reporting is static and there is no dependency-aware readiness boundary
evidence: bootstrap/application.py /healthz returns status=ok without checking DB, Artifact store, Session store or Connector readiness
ObjectStorageArtifactBlobStore.initialize() is a no-op
no product /readyz, /livez or /metrics route was found
findings.impact: A process can report healthy before an Object Storage credential/bucket failure is discovered on first use; orchestration cannot distinguish liveness from readiness.
findings.recommended_closure: Separate liveness/readiness, add bounded dependency probes with secret-safe diagnostics, and define readiness ownership for PostgreSQL, Artifact storage and required external connectors.

findings.title: Service bearer-token registry is static startup JSON with no expiry/revocation/rotation lifecycle
evidence: ServiceClientTokenRegistry accepts only token_id, token_sha256, tenant_id, principal_id and roles
registry is loaded from environment at startup and has no expiry, not-before, revoked-at, issuer/audience or dynamic reload fields
findings.impact: Credential replacement requires process/config rotation and there is no first-class revocation or validity window.
findings.recommended_closure: For production use, integrate an external identity boundary such as OIDC/JWT validation or add a durable revocation-aware rotating registry while retaining tenant/principal/role ownership checks.

findings.title: Artifact orphan inventory, quarantine and garbage collection are not representable through current ports
evidence: ArtifactBlobStorePort exposes initialize/put/read/verify/delete/exists only; no listing or age metadata
ArtifactService performs immediate compensating delete only when metadata registration raises
ProductStore exposes per-Run artifact listing but no global storage-reference inventory/removal lifecycle
findings.impact: A crash after blob put or a failed compensation can leave a blob that no durable inventory process can discover and safely reap.
findings.recommended_closure: After MinIO live semantics are accepted, add bounded blob inventory plus durable metadata inventory, orphan age threshold, quarantine/recheck and idempotent deletion.

findings.title: S3-compatible client relies on SDK defaults for timeout/retry/TLS/encryption policy
evidence: S3CompatibleClientSettings owns endpoint_url, region_name and addressing_style only
botocore Config explicitly sets signature_version and addressing_style but no Product-owned retry/timeout policy
no Product-owned server-side encryption policy or custom CA/TLS policy is represented
findings.impact: Behavior can vary by SDK/default environment and operational requirements such as bounded retries, private CA trust and encryption-at-rest are not part of the Product contract.
findings.recommended_closure: Do not change before MinIO live evidence. Then define explicit bounded client policy and deployment contract based on observed S3-compatible behavior.

findings.title: Durable claim/expiry/recovery state exists, but execution remains single-process and has no heartbeat/lease renewal
evidence: LocalExecutionCoordinator explicitly states single-process and uses asyncio.create_task
Submission lifecycle defaults to explicit-local-operator recovery and rejects distributed_worker_lease_enabled
existing submission persistence already contains claim owner/token/acquired/expires/recovery fields
findings.impact: The current process cannot provide multi-worker ownership, liveness renewal or automatic lost-worker recovery.
findings.recommended_closure: Extend the existing ledger; do not build a second claim system. Add physical Worker, lease renewal/heartbeat, lost-worker reconciliation and forced-termination acceptance.

findings.title: Session metadata is PostgreSQL-capable but actual model conversation history remains node-local encrypted SQLite
evidence: STEP091B3 design retains encrypted local SQLite for SDK Session history
session history TTL is deliberately disabled
distributed Session history remains explicitly unimplemented
findings.impact: A conversation cannot transparently move between Worker nodes without an explicit history ownership/migration strategy.
findings.recommended_closure: Select only with API/Worker/HA work: define distributed history ownership or sticky session placement plus failure recovery and retention policy.

findings.title: Enterprise write routing exists only as proposal-only policy; governed write execution is absent
evidence: assistant_routing/service.py routes enterprise-action-write-v1 with proposal_only=True
RuntimeInfo reports groupware_action_agent_implemented=False and groupware_action_mcp_server_implemented=False
Groupware Connector exposes read-only tools only
findings.impact: The runtime can identify write intent but cannot execute a governed enterprise mutation.
findings.recommended_closure: Follow Master Plan Phase 3: separate action Agent/MCP credentials, durable Command ledger, hash-bound Approval, idempotency/expected revision, unknown-outcome reconciliation and read-after-write verification.

findings.title: Durable automation routing exists only as proposal-only policy; scheduler/registry are absent
evidence: assistant_routing/service.py maps durable-automation-v1 with reason durable-scheduler-not-configured and proposal_only=True
RuntimeInfo reports groupware_read_durable_automation_enabled=False and organization_assistant_durable_automation_configured=False
no Product automation registry/scheduler package was found
findings.impact: Users cannot create restart-safe scheduled or condition-watch work despite the routing vocabulary already existing.
findings.recommended_closure: Implement a durable Automation registry that creates governed Submissions, schedule/condition dedupe, restart-safe firing and execution-time approval.

findings.title: Read-only Groupware/Organization connector foundations exist, but real enterprise-provider deployment evidence remains incomplete
evidence: Groupware connector is read-only and local/fake acceptance-oriented
RuntimeInfo retains false flags for production external provider/OAuth/live configuration
findings.impact: Local/fake evidence does not prove actual private-network provider credentials, OAuth refresh, tenant routing or provider SLA behavior.
findings.recommended_closure: Treat as deployment acceptance, not a rewrite: add vendor profile, secret ownership, OAuth refresh if required and actual enterprise read live gate.

findings.title: Production metrics, backup/restore gates, SBOM/dependency lock and deployment automation are not repository-owned
evidence: Master Plan Phase 9 still lists metrics, backup/restore, load/soak/failure injection, SBOM and dependency audit
no product metrics route or OpenTelemetry/Prometheus integration was found
no transitive Python lock file was found; pyproject uses ranges for most dependencies and sh_setup.cmd installs editable current constraints
no first-party CI workflow, Dockerfile, Helm or Terraform artifact was found in the audited repository
findings.impact: Build/deploy reproducibility and operational recovery remain dependent on external/manual procedures.
findings.recommended_closure: Before production gate, choose owned deployment boundary, freeze resolved dependencies, produce SBOM/security audit, and add backup/restore plus load/soak evidence.

findings.title: Several orchestration functions and the historical acceptance surface are highly concentrated
evidence: generic_gateway.py run() is about 1,650 lines
runtime_binding.py resolve() is about 1,034 lines
execution/service.py execute_prepared() is about 702 lines
first-party Runtime scripts are about 67.9k Python lines versus about 49.4k Product/Protocol/Client Python lines
189 .cmd launchers exist in the package
findings.impact: Current-step identity, launcher and manifest regressions have repeatedly occurred and large functions raise change impact.
findings.recommended_closure: Do not refactor blindly. First centralize current-step identity/launcher generation and strengthen SOT gates; then split large orchestration functions only along existing tested policy/adapter boundaries.

findings.title: Product Web/Approval/Automation UI and Skill Platform V2 remain planned
evidence: Master Plan Phase 7 calls for versioned Skill registry and bounded Skill search
Master Plan Phase 8 calls for Conversation/Run/Artifact/Approval/Automation Product UI
current Service CLI exists but runtime browser surfaces are development harnesses
findings.impact: Core runtime capabilities are not yet exposed as the intended end-user Product surface.
findings.recommended_closure: Do after production execution boundaries are stable; Client must consume Service API and persisted canonical state only.

findings.title: Automatic model retry/fallback is intentionally disabled
evidence: RuntimeInfo model policy sets automatic fallback false and runner/provider max retries to zero
findings.impact: Transient provider errors are surfaced rather than automatically retried; this is safer for side-effect correctness but limits resilience.
findings.recommended_closure: Keep disabled until replay and side-effect safety are proven; if enabled later, use category-bounded retry with persisted attempt evidence.

recommended_order: MinIO/real Object Storage STEP091D live acceptance when environment is ready
R7-AUDIT-006/R7-AUDIT-007 Artifact orphan lifecycle and Object Storage operational hardening
R7-AUDIT-008/R7-AUDIT-009 API/Worker, lease/heartbeat and distributed Session/HA
non_findings: No evidence supports rebuilding PostgreSQL claim/admission ownership; durable claim/expiry/recovery fields already exist.
No evidence supports implementing Artifact GC before Object Storage live semantics are accepted.
No evidence supports enabling automatic model retry/fallback now; it is intentionally disabled for side-effect safety.
No product source TODO/FIXME/NotImplementedError stubs were found in audited first-party Product packages.
